pwc.title: PwC Switzerland virtual case
pwc.intro: An Excel and Power BI modeling portfolio based on the PwC Switzerland virtual case experience hosted on Forage.
pwc.problem: Call-center operations, customer retention, and workforce questions require different fact grains and clearly defined KPIs. Combining the domains needs shared dimensions without losing those differences.
approach: Organize telephony, retention, and workforce data into a galaxy semantic model.
Use Power Query for transformation and Power Pivot / VertiPaq for analytical modeling.
Define DAX measures and build domain-specific reporting views.
Develop workbook navigation and VBA controls around the reporting experience.
pwc.takeaway: Explore the semantic-model documentation, KPI catalog, Power Query transformations, and VBA modules. The project shows how spreadsheet delivery can be structured and versioned.
pwc.caveat: This is a virtual case experience and portfolio exercise, not employment at PwC or a client engagement.
pwc.stack: Excel · Power Query · Power Pivot · DAX · VBA

customer360.title: Customer 360 banking ETL
customer360.intro: A banking integration capstone combining relational customer data with ATM and credit-card files using Informatica Cloud Data Integration.
customer360.problem: Customer information and transaction records arrive from separate systems. Invalid identifiers and account conditions need explicit routing before creating a consolidated customer view.
approach: Join Oracle banking entities with ATM and credit-card flat-file inputs.
Normalize customer names and enforce a documented exception matrix.
Quarantine non-conforming records with descriptive rejection reasons.
Aggregate customer-level spending and use an upsert delivery pattern.
customer360.takeaway: The mapping and exception documentation make the difference between ingestion and trustworthy integration visible. Review the routing rules and customer-grain output.
customer360.caveat: Academic capstone scenario; no claim of access to real bank customer records or a live banking deployment.
customer360.stack: Informatica IICS · Oracle · CSV · ETL · Data quality

supplychain.title: SMART Supply Chain Insights
supplychain.intro: A supply-chain analysis project connecting Python exploration, Excel modeling, and Power BI reporting.
supplychain.problem: Sales, fulfillment, shipping risk, and suspicious or cancelled orders need to be explored together to understand operational patterns.
approach: Clean and explore the supplied transaction dataset with Python.
Investigate distributions, sales and profit trends, and order-status patterns.
Develop a star-schema model and relationships.
Build Power BI views using DAX and interactive reporting.
supplychain.takeaway: Follow the repository from raw data and EDA to model design and report artifacts. It shows the analytical work behind an operations dashboard.
supplychain.caveat: Repository dataset and analytical findings do not establish realized operational savings or a client engagement.
supplychain.stack: Python · Pandas · Excel · Power BI · DAX
supplychain.dataset_context: The repository identifies the DataCo supply-chain dataset and includes the source data, field descriptions, a cleaned workbook, an exploratory notebook, a dimensional-model workbook, and Power BI artifacts. Its documented period is 2015–2018, covering 65,752 orders, 20,652 customers, and 118 products.
supplychain.contribution: Prepared and explored the data with Python and Pandas, organized cleaned data and a dimensional model in Excel, and built a five-page Power BI reporting experience with DAX measures.
supplychain.model: A star-schema model with a DAX calendar table and time-intelligence measures including month-to-date, quarter-to-date, year-to-date, and rolling metrics.
supplychain.findings: The report provides separate views for order fulfillment, customer and market patterns, product profitability, shipping operations, and time trends. The repository does not establish realized operational savings or a client deployment.

retail.title: B2B Retail Analytics & Churn Diagnostic — Portfolio Scenario
retail.intro: A Power BI portfolio scenario exploring retailer lifecycle, delivery performance, sales movement, and category mix in an Egyptian B2B grocery-distribution context.
retail.problem: A change in sales can have several causes. Retention, delivery performance, and commercial mix need separate definitions and a shared reporting model before they can be reviewed together.
approach: Organize the analytical entities and transaction facts in a star-schema model.
Define DAX measures for performance, period comparisons, retailer activity, and lifecycle analysis.
Explore delivery SLA, cohort retention, activation, and sales-drop decomposition.
Arrange the report around executive, operations, retention, and commercial questions.
retail.takeaway: The report is designed to direct a review toward retailer retention, delivery performance, sales movement, or category mix. These are intended decision areas, not measured business outcomes.
retail.caveat: This is an independent portfolio scenario, not a client engagement. No employment, private company data access, verified operational impact, or real-world deployment is claimed.
retail.stack: Power BI · DAX · SQL Server · Star schema
retail.dataset_context: The project is presented as an Egyptian B2B grocery-distribution portfolio scenario. The repository documents its report and implementation artifacts; no private client dataset provenance is asserted.
retail.contribution: The repository documents the Power BI report, SQL and Power Query preparation, semantic-model design, and DAX measures used to explore retailer lifecycle and commercial performance.
retail.model: A star-schema reporting model with measures for active retailers, purchase frequency, inactivity-based churn, cohort retention, delivery performance, and category movement.
retail.findings: The report separates lifecycle, delivery, and commercial signals so that each can be examined on its own terms. It does not report a measured change in a real business.

deepclean.title: DeepClean OS
deepclean.intro: A Python data-preparation toolkit with a Streamlit interface for exploring a repeatable cleaning sequence.
deepclean.problem: Data preparation often spreads across ad-hoc notebook cells. A reusable pipeline can make the chosen transformations easier to inspect and repeat.
approach: Organize duplicate removal and temporal feature handling into separate stages.
Provide configurable imputation, outlier treatment, encoding, and scaling.
Expose a Python engine alongside an interactive Streamlit interface.
Document the transformation order and dependencies.
deepclean.takeaway: Explore the modular cleaning implementation and interface. Each transformation should be selected for the dataset and business question; an automated sequence is a tool, not a universal cleaning policy.
deepclean.caveat: A portfolio data-preparation tool. Statistical imputation or outlier treatment may be inappropriate for a particular dataset without domain review.
deepclean.stack: Python · Pandas · NumPy · scikit-learn · SciPy · Streamlit

stockpipeline.title: Stock-price data pipeline
stockpipeline.intro: An automated market-data pipeline connecting Airflow orchestration, Spark processing, object storage, PostgreSQL, and Metabase.
stockpipeline.problem: API availability, raw-data retention, transformation, loading, and delivery need explicit boundaries for a pipeline to be understandable and repeatable.
approach: Check API availability and ingest price data into MinIO raw storage.
Run Spark transformation in a Docker task.
Load the formatted output into a PostgreSQL warehouse.
Connect Metabase reporting and workflow completion notifications.
stockpipeline.takeaway: Read the DAG and architecture documentation to follow dependencies from ingestion to reporting. The project highlights the orchestration around an analytical dataset.
stockpipeline.caveat: A technical portfolio pipeline. The website does not provide live market data, investment advice, or a verified throughput benchmark.
stockpipeline.stack: Airflow · Spark · MinIO · PostgreSQL · Metabase · Docker

insurance.title: National Insurance data warehouse
insurance.intro: An Egyptian Form 5 portfolio scenario covering synthetic data generation, cleaning, orchestration, SQL Server warehousing, and Power BI.
insurance.problem: Insurance-style records involve dates, repeated entities, and validation constraints. A useful warehouse needs consistent processing and explicit analytical views.
approach: Generate synthetic source records for the documented scenario.
Normalize datatypes, handle duplicates, and validate records.
Orchestrate processing and loading with Airflow.
Create SQL Server warehouse structures and analytical views for reporting.
insurance.takeaway: Inspect the generation, cleaning, loading, and SQL-validation modules as one connected workflow. The project puts local domain context into a reproducible learning scenario.
insurance.caveat: All identity and insurance records in the scenario are synthetic. This is not an official government system or access to real insurance records.
insurance.stack: Python · Pandas · Airflow · SQL Server · Power BI · Docker

eur-egp.title: EUR to EGP Rate Monitor
eur-egp.intro: A scheduled n8n workflow that monitors indicative EUR/EGP bank rates, detects fresh directional changes, and sends AI-assisted Telegram notifications.
eur-egp.problem: Checking a currency feed repeatedly does not reveal whether either directional bank rate has changed, whether the observation is fresh, or whether a stale response should be ignored. The workflow needs a persistent baseline and explicit routing rules to avoid duplicate or misleading alerts.
approach: Fetch the Daleelak EUR feed every five minutes and validate the EUR-EGP asset, numeric rates, bank labels, and observation metadata.
Keep the customer-sells-EUR and customer-buys-EUR rates separate, then compare each with the previous values stored in an n8n Data Table.
Round rate differences to two decimal places and allow notifications only when a rate changed and the source is marked fresh and not stale.
Use OpenRouter to generate a short explanation from the validated comparison, then deliver the rate details and summary through Telegram.
Advance the baseline only after Telegram delivery succeeds; let unchanged or stale observations end without notification or baseline mutation.
eur-egp.takeaway: The project brings together API ingestion, validation, stateful change detection, conditional orchestration, AI-assisted explanation, and notification delivery. The repository includes the sanitized importable workflow, architecture diagram, data dictionary, and setup/testing checklist.
eur-egp.caveat: This portfolio workflow reads an indicative public feed and sends notifications. It does not guarantee executable bank quotes, execute financial transactions, provide financial advice, or establish third-party uptime. The owner verified both workflow branches and baseline restoration on 10 November 2026; that test record is not a claim of continuous service reliability.
eur-egp.stack: n8n · JavaScript · Daleelak API · n8n Data Tables · OpenRouter · Telegram

commonwealth.title: Commonwealth Bank — Introduction to Data Science
commonwealth.intro: A completed four-task Forage simulation connecting transaction analysis, privacy-aware customer-data preparation, social-media insights, and relational database design.
commonwealth.problem: The exercises span different analytical responsibilities: answering business questions from transaction-level records, preparing a useful but privacy-conscious customer release, interpreting social-media interactions, and proposing a structure that preserves post and account relationships.
approach: Used Excel Tables, structured references, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, data-quality checks, and PivotTables to analyse 50,783 supermarket transaction records and independently reconcile five business metrics.

Prepared a four-column values-only release from 10,000 customer records by removing direct identifiers, generalising registration dates, creating age and salary bands, and reviewing quasi-identifier group sizes and salary-band diversity.

Analysed 60 fictional social-media posts with Excel formulas and PivotTables; reviewed the actual text of all 11 records flagged for a response, assessed X API feasibility, and completed the InsightSpark proposal.
Designed a normalised relational model with Accounts, Posts, Post_References, Post_Mentions, Hashtags, and Post_Hashtags, plus optional media, metric-snapshot, and analysis extensions.
commonwealth.takeaway: The project shows how careful Excel work can move beyond calculation into quality checks, privacy-aware preparation, evidence-based interpretation, and a database design that protects the grain and relationships of the source information.
commonwealth.caveat: This is a completed Forage virtual job simulation, not employment at Commonwealth Bank or a paid client engagement. The Task 03 social-media records and engagement values are fictional. X API research was a feasibility exercise, sentiment labels were supplied by the simulation, and Task 04 is a proposed schema rather than a deployed database.
commonwealth.stack: Microsoft Excel · Excel Tables · SUMIFS / COUNTIFS · PivotTables · Data Quality · Data Privacy · Relational Database Design

wuzzuf.title: Egypt’s Data Job Market
wuzzuf.intro: A Power BI report exploring a saved January–March 2025 snapshot of job postings collected from Wuzzuf in Egypt.
wuzzuf.problem: Which roles and skills appear in the collected postings, where is hiring activity visible, and how should the available salary information be interpreted?
approach: Use the prepared job-posting and salary extracts documented in the repository.
Structure the report around job roles, requested skills, companies, locations, salaries, and job duration.
Use DAX measures, interactive slicers, dynamic titles, conditional formatting, and tooltip pages to support exploration.
Keep the saved report snapshot and the limitations of the source extracts visible when interpreting the results.
wuzzuf.takeaway: In the documented report snapshot, Data Analyst is the most frequent job title, AI is the most requested skill, and New Cairo is the top hiring city. These are observations from the supplied snapshot, not current labour-market statistics.
wuzzuf.caveat: The report covers 217 postings collected during January–March 2025. Salary data is incomplete, the original Python collection source is not included in the tracked repository, and no automatic refresh schedule is documented.
wuzzuf.dataset_context: A saved extract of 217 Wuzzuf job postings collected in Egypt during January–March 2025, alongside salary-related Excel data. The repository contains prepared Excel extracts and the Power BI report.
wuzzuf.contribution: The repository documents a Python-based collection workflow, prepared Excel data extracts, and the Power BI report. The tracked repository does not include the original collection script.
wuzzuf.model: A Power BI reporting model with DAX measures, interactive slicers, dynamic titles, conditional formatting, tooltip pages, and geographic visuals.
wuzzuf.findings: The README records Data Analyst as the most common title, AI as the most requested skill, and New Cairo as the leading city in this particular dataset snapshot. Salary observations depend on the incomplete salary records.
